# Evidence tables

Certainty reflects the strength and consistency of the underlying evidence
(GRADE-style judgement), not the size of the effect. `Status` separates
established findings from emerging or unsupported ones. A real but tiny
effect can be established and still be clinically unimportant.

| Does a larger dose deliver proportionally more magnesium? | Efficiency of absorption | Balance studies and reviews; Multiple studies | Fractional absorption declines with dose; split doses are absorbed better | Moderate | Established | R08 |

| Does L-threonate deliver magnesium to the brain? | Brain magnesium concentration | Animal studies plus small human trials; Preclinical | Raises brain magnesium in animals; human brain magnesium has not been measured | Very low | Emerging | R34, R37 |
| Is malate better absorbed or more effective? | Comparative bioavailability | No head-to-head trials; 0 trials | No human comparative data | Very low | Unsupported | R09 |
| Is magnesium taurate cardioprotective? | Cardiovascular outcomes | No outcome trials of the salt; 0 trials | No outcome data for magnesium taurate | Very low | Unsupported | R09, R52 |
| Is magnesium chloride well absorbed? | Fractional absorption | Randomised crossover; 1 trial; 16 adults | 9-11% absorbed, versus 4% for oxide | Moderate | Established | R03 |
| Do Epsom salt baths raise magnesium status? | Serum and urinary magnesium | Small uncontrolled and ex vivo studies; Multiple | Inconsistent small changes; intact skin is nearly impermeable to magnesium | Very low | Unsupported | R38, R40 |
| Does transdermal magnesium cream raise serum magnesium? | Serum magnesium | Pilot randomised placebo-controlled trial; 1 trial; 25 participants | 0.82 to 0.89 mmol/L, not significant overall (p=0.29) | Very low | Mixed | R39 |

## Deficiency and status assessment

| Question | Outcome | Evidence base | Result | Certainty | Status | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Does serum magnesium reflect body stores? | Diagnostic accuracy | Physiology and laboratory review | Less than 1% of body magnesium is in serum; normal range 0.75-0.95 mmol/L | High | Established | R01, R56 |
| How common is low magnesium intake? | Intake below the Estimated Average Requirement | National survey; NHANES 2013-2016 | 48% below the EAR | Moderate | Established | R01 |
| Can a normal serum level exclude deficiency? | Diagnostic accuracy | Review | Normal serum does not exclude intracellular depletion | Moderate | Established | R51 |
| Who is at risk of magnesium inadequacy? | Risk factors | Government review | Gastrointestinal disease, type 2 diabetes, alcohol dependence, older age, diuretics and PPIs | Moderate | Established | R01 |
| Is magnesium status routinely tested? | Testing practice | Government review | Not measured in NHANES since 1974; not part of routine electrolytes | Moderate | Established | R01 |

## Safety, toxicity and interactions

| Question | Outcome | Evidence base | Result | Certainty | Status | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| At what serum level does toxicity appear? | Clinical signs | Clinical review | 1.74-2.61 mmol/L, progressing to respiratory depression and cardiac arrest | Moderate | Established | R01, R45 |
| Who develops hypermagnesemia on oral magnesium? | Serum magnesium | Retrospective cohort; 320 patients | eGFR 55.4 or below OR 3.1; MgO 1650 mg/day or more OR 1.9; 36 days or more OR 2.2 | Moderate | Established | R43 |
| Can oral magnesium be fatal? | Case reports | Case series; 2 cases | 3000 mg/day hydroxide in end-stage renal disease reached 9.9 mg/dL; a patient with normal renal function reached 11.0 mg/dL and died | Low | Established | R44 |
| Which forms cause diarrhoea? | Gastrointestinal adverse events | Government review and trials | Carbonate, chloride, gluconate and oxide most reported; citrate is dose-dependent | Moderate | Established | R01, R19 |
| Do proton pump inhibitors cause hypomagnesemia? | Serum magnesium | FDA safety review | Hypomagnesemia after typically more than a year; supplements corrected levels in most reviewed cases | Moderate | Established | R41 |
| How should magnesium be spaced from antibiotics? | Absorption interaction | Pharmacokinetic review | Tetracyclines and quinolones: take magnesium 2 hours before or 4-6 hours after | Moderate | Established | R01 |
| Does magnesium reduce bisphosphonate absorption? | Absorption | Pharmacokinetic review | Separate by at least 2 hours | Moderate | Established | R01 |
| Do high zinc doses affect magnesium? | Magnesium balance | Balance study; 1 study | 142 mg/day zinc interfered with magnesium absorption and balance | Low | Emerging | R01 |
| Is magnesium safe in chronic kidney disease? | Serum magnesium | Clinical review | Accumulation risk; monitoring required; dialysis patients need individualised targets | Moderate | Established | R42, R54 |
